lessons.title: F and J, the index fingers
lessons.tip: Welcome! Rest your index fingers on F (left hand) and J (right hand). These are your two guide keys, each with a small bump. Do not look at your keyboard: trust your muscle memory.

tuto.intro: Welcome to your very first lesson! Take 30 seconds to learn the basics of touch typing with ten fingers. It will change everything from here on.

rules.d: Rest your eight fingers on the middle row: A S D F for the left hand, J K L ; for the right hand. Your index fingers go on F and J, where you can feel a small bump. It is how you find your place without ever looking down.

rules.t: Keep your eyes on the screen
rules.d: Do not look at your fingers. Learning to stop looking at the keyboard is how you build the muscle memory that makes you truly fast.
Use your thumb for the long bar at the bottom, either one, whichever you prefer. A quick tap between groups of letters is all it takes.
Type slowly and accurately: every mistake builds a bad habit. Speed will come by itself once the movement is memorised.

tuto.tip: Goal: anchor your two index fingers by typing only F and J. Do not force it. Aim for steadiness, not speed.

lessons.title: D and K, the middle fingers
lessons.tip: Your middle fingers rest naturally on D and K, right next to your index fingers. Keep your index fingers on F and J as anchors: every finger returns to its home key after each keystroke.

tuto.intro: Now add your middle fingers. D and K sit right next to your index fingers, on the same home row.

rules.d: Your left middle finger covers D and your right middle finger covers K. They rest naturally on these keys, right beside F and J.
Do not move your index fingers: they stay on F and J while your middle fingers type. This is what lets you find your way back without looking.
A light press is enough. Do not lift your whole hand: just let the finger drop down, then come back up to its place.

tuto.tip: Goal: type F D K J from memory, keeping all four fingers close to their home positions.

lessons.title: S and L, the ring fingers
lessons.tip: Your ring fingers cover S and L. That is six fingers in place now. Think of a gentle arch: your fingers rest slightly curved, ready to strike without lifting your wrist.

tuto.intro: Place your ring fingers on S (left) and L (right). You now have six fingers resting on the home row.

rules.d: Ring fingers are less agile than your index and middle fingers, and that is normal. Go slowly: accuracy comes before speed.
Keep your fingers slightly curved, as if resting on a small ball. Your wrist stays relaxed and does not sink onto the desk.
After every S or L, the ring finger goes back to its place. Your index fingers on F and J remain your guides.

tuto.tip: Goal: type S and L without twisting your hand, returning to the home row every time.

lessons.title: A and semicolon, the little fingers
lessons.tip: Your little fingers are the weakest, and that is normal. A on the left, semicolon on the right. Do not turn your whole wrist: just let the little finger stretch a little.

tuto.intro: Now for the little fingers: A on the left, semicolon on the right. They are the trickiest to tame. With them, your home row is complete: A S D F, then J K L ;.

rules.d: Your little fingers lack strength and precision at first. Everyone starts here, even the pros. Be patient.

rules.t: Do not drag the whole hand
rules.d: Only stretch the little finger towards A or ;. If you swivel your wrist, your other fingers lose their place.
The little finger tends to stay in the air. Bring it back to its home key as soon as it has struck.

tuto.tip: Goal: bring your little fingers into action without breaking your home position. Go slowly and stay steady.

lessons.title: G and H, the inner index fingers
lessons.tip: G and H are typed by your index fingers stretching slightly towards the centre. Keep the movement small: the finger slides, it does not jump. Return to F or J after each keystroke.

tuto.intro: G and H are in the middle of the keyboard. Your index fingers stretch a little to reach them.

rules.d: Your left index finger slides right for G, and your right index finger slides left for H. It is a small sideways movement, not a jump.
Straight after G or H, bring your index finger back to its home key. These are the home-row keys furthest from your starting position.

rules.t: Do not mix up the hands
rules.d: G is always typed with the left index finger, and H always with the right. Keep this rule firmly in mind.

tuto.tip: Goal: cover the whole middle of the home row without moving your other fingers.

lessons.title: Review: the whole home row
lessons.keys: a s d f g h j k l ;
lessons.tip: A full review of the home row. This is your base: all your fingers return here after every keystroke. Take your time: steadiness matters more than speed.

tuto.intro: You now know the whole home row, the row your fingers always come back to between keystrokes.

rules.d: All your fingers start from this row and return to it. Mastering it means knowing where you are on the keyboard without looking.
This exercise mixes all ten keys. If you hesitate, slow down: the aim is to find them from memory, not to type fast.
Between keystrokes, feel that your eight fingers have gone back to A S D F and J K L ;.

tuto.tip: Goal: pass the whole home row with your fingers anchored and your eyes on the screen.
